directAnswer: Pope Clement XI was Giovanni Francesco Albani of Urbino, who reigned from 23 November 1700 to 19 March 1721, one of the longer pontificates of the era. He issued the bull Unigenitus against Jansenism, ruled against the Chinese Rites, made the feast of the Immaculate Conception a holy day for the whole Church, and steered the papacy through the War of the Spanish Succession.

sections.h2: A Reluctant Pope Elected at Fifty-One
paras: Giovanni Francesco Albani was born in Urbino in 1649 and was known as a gifted Latinist and scholar. He held a series of Curial posts, was made a cardinal in 1690, and became an influential drafter of papal documents. Notably, he had been ordained a priest only shortly before the conclave of 1700.

Elected at fifty-one, young by the standards of the time, Albani reportedly hesitated for days before accepting. His reign began just as the death of the childless Charles II of Spain set off a struggle among the European powers for the Spanish throne.

Jansenism, with its stern views of grace and its resistance to Roman authority, remained a source of division in France. In 1705 Clement XI issued Vineam Domini, which rejected the Jansenist tactic of 'respectful silence' toward earlier condemnations. In 1713 he issued the constitution Unigenitus, condemning 101 propositions from the Moral Reflections on the New Testament by Pasquier Quesnel.

Unigenitus became one of the most contested papal documents of the eighteenth century. A group of French bishops and clergy appealed against it to a future general council, and the controversy over its acceptance shaped French Church life for decades after Clement's death.

Jesuit missionaries in China had allowed converts to keep certain ceremonies honoring Confucius and ancestors, judging them civil rather than religious. Other missionaries disagreed. After long investigation, Clement XI approved a decree in 1704 forbidding the practices, sent a legate, Charles-Thomas Maillard de Tournon, to China, and in 1715 issued the bull Ex illa die requiring missionaries to swear obedience to the ruling.

The decision provoked opposition from the Kangxi Emperor and seriously hindered missionary work in China. The question was settled definitively only in the twentieth century, when Pius XII in 1939 permitted Chinese Catholics to take part in such civil ceremonies.

During the War of the Spanish Succession the Papal States were caught between the Bourbon and Habsburg camps. Imperial troops occupied papal territory, including Comacchio, and Clement was forced in 1709 to recognize the Habsburg claimant Charles as king of Spain, angering the Bourbons. The Peace of Utrecht later disposed of Italian lands with little regard for papal claims.

Clement XI's devotional legacy endures. In 1708 he extended the feast of the Immaculate Conception on December 8 to the universal Church as a holy day of obligation, and after the Christian victory over the Ottomans at Petrovaradin in 1716 he extended the feast of the Holy Rosary to the whole Church. He also sent scholars to collect Eastern manuscripts for the Vatican Library and encouraged study of Rome's Christian antiquities.

keyFacts: Born Giovanni Francesco Albani in Urbino in 1649
Issued Unigenitus (1713) condemning 101 propositions of Quesnel
Ruled against the Chinese Rites, confirmed in Ex illa die (1715)
Made the Immaculate Conception (December 8) a universal feast in 1708
Extended the feast of the Holy Rosary to the universal Church in 1716

faqs.question: What was the bull Unigenitus?
faqs.answer: Unigenitus, issued by Clement XI in 1713, condemned 101 propositions from Pasquier Quesnel's Jansenist-leaning commentary on the New Testament. It caused prolonged controversy in France, where some clergy appealed against it.

faqs.question: Why did Clement XI forbid the Chinese Rites?
faqs.answer: After long study he concluded that ceremonies honoring Confucius and ancestors, as then practiced, were incompatible with Christian worship. His rulings of 1704 and 1715 were relaxed only in 1939 under Pius XII.

faqs.question: What did Clement XI do for the feast of the Immaculate Conception?
faqs.answer: In 1708 he extended the December 8 feast of the Immaculate Conception to the entire Church as a holy day of obligation, nearly 150 years before Pius IX defined the doctrine as dogma.
